subject: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:14:00 -04:00
Subject: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the quick demo yesterday — the throughput profiles looked promising. Procurement asked me to follow up with specific questions so we can evaluate pricing and contract options:

- Can you send a short matrix with the uptime tiers you support (99.5 / 99.9 / 99.99) and the corresponding response windows and typical credit calculations?
- For large committed spend (we're looking at a 3-year, multi-region deployment, estimate ~$1.2M ARR), do you offer a volume rebate or stepped discounts tied to committed GPU-hours or token volumes? How do seat-based user licenses interact with those rebates?
- Escalation coverage: we need a clear description of on-call coverage (hours, follow-the-sun vs regional), escalation SLAs for Sev1/Sev2, and whether 24/7 engineering involvement is included for higher tiers.

Also, please attach any standard SLA exhibits and the redline template your legal team prefers. Procurement would like to see credit caps and liability language up front to feed to our counsel.

Thanks — Jordan
Director of Platform Ops | Acme Corp
[attachment requested: SOC2 report, network diagrams]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage

Jordan — great to hear from you and glad the demo was useful. Attaching a compact matrix that maps the three uptime bands we commonly propose to customers and the baseline credit approach. High level answers below:

- Uptime tiers: 99.5% / 99.9% / 99.99%. Response windows: Standard (business hours) next-business-hour triage for low tiers; 4-hour Sev2 / 1-hour Sev1 for mid tiers; 30-minute Sev1 / 2-hour Sev2 and 24/7 follow-the-sun for top tier. See attached SLA_Options_Matrix_v1.xlsx for the grid with examples.
- Credits: credits are percentage-of-monthly-invoice slabs tied to minutes of downtime; we cap cumulative credits at 100% of monthly fees per incident window and 300% annually for managed customers. For enterprise committed deals we can negotiate higher caps and different credit multipliers — legal can provide a tailored exhibit.
- Volume rebates: we offer stepped rebates based on committed annual spend or GPU-hour commitments. Example: 10% rebate band at $500k ARR, 18% at $1M, 25% at $1.5M (these are illustrative). Seat-based pricing is additive for named seat support; rebates apply to consumption lines (tokens/GPU hours) and we can provide blended pricing for seat-heavy contracts.
- Escalation/coverage: top-tier includes 24/7 engineering escalation, designated escalation path, and an assigned Technical Account Manager. Mid-tier covers extended-hours engineering on-call.

I've looped in Ben and Rishi to help with legal/ops items and to propose contract language and an example exhibit.

Next step: can you confirm whether Acme needs a 3-year firm term with multi-region (us + eu) or if the first phase is US-only? That will materially change the rebate math.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA_Options_Matrix_v1.xlsx]
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:47:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage

Marissa — thanks, matrix received. A couple quick clarifications from Procurement and our CTO:

- We're targeting a 3-year commitment but would prefer to stage region expansion: year 1 US only, year 2 add EU, year 3 APAC. Can rebate bands be trued up annually based on regional activation?
- For the top-tier 24/7 option, can you confirm whether the 24/7 engineering escalation includes dedicated shift rotations (i.e., guaranteed engineer in the rotation for our account) or if it's on-demand from the pool? If it's pooled, can we get an SLA on max handoff time to a named engineer?
- If we accept a slightly lower uptime (99.9 vs 99.99) would Redwood be willing to move the seat license fee into the consumption bucket (to simplify invoicing) and increase the volume rebate by +3%?

Also, our counsel will want to see suggested liability/credit caps before we go to signatures. Appreciate you and the team tackling this quickly.

— Jordan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 08:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage

Looping Ben (Legal) and Rishi (Solutions/Delivery) to confirm the operational and contract-side details. Internal notes below (Ben/Rishi, please chime in and feel free to redline):

- Regional true-up: we can structure the rebate schedule with annual truing based on which regions are ramped. We'll need to lock a committed baseline for year 1 and a mechanism for binding expansion options for years 2/3. Pricing team can provide a staged table.
- 24/7 engineering: Rishi — can you confirm whether we can offer a named-engineer rotation for Acme at this deal size, or whether we must provide pooled 24/7 with guaranteed escalation targets? If pooled, what's the SLO to reach a named SME?
- Seat-to-consumption swap: this is doable commercially but requires invoicing/entitlement changes. Finance will need to sign off on revenue recognition and seat-to-consumption adjustments for rebates.

Ben — procurement asked for liability/credit caps. Suggest we propose the standard enterprise exhibit but offer to relax the annual credit cap for a larger commitment. If you can prepare a redline with alternate caps (e.g., 300% annual default, up to 500% for committed deals) that will help negotiations.

Action items: Rishi to confirm operational coverage; Ben to provide a redline; Marissa to circulate a revised pricing table with staged rebates.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage

Jordan/Marissa — quick legal take and proposed redlines attached. Key points:

- Liability / credits: we typically cap aggregate service credits at 300% of the monthly fees and carve out consequential damages, subject to negotiated exceptions. For a multi-year committed ARR at the $1M+ band we can consider increasing the annual credit cap to 400–500% and adding a fixed sum liability floor in serious breach scenarios.
- Named-engineer rotations: operational detail rather than legal, but if we commit to a named rotation we need to set clear replacement and notice terms (SLAs for handoffs, max single-person single-point-of-failure mitigations).
- Invoicing model: moving seat fees into consumption is commercial; we need explicit language about entitlement reconciliation and annual true-ups to avoid revenue recognition disputes.

I've attached SLA_terms_redline.docx with alternate paragraphs highlighted (credit caps, named-engineer appendix, invoicing/true-up). If Acme is comfortable with the higher annual credit cap we should reflect that as a commercial concession in the quote.

Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA_terms_redline.docx]
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@acme.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acme.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA packaging: options, volume rebates & escalation coverage

Jordan — thanks for the clarifying questions and Ben/Rishi for fast responses. Summary / next steps:

1) Commercial: I'll send a staged quote that shows year-by-year pricing and an illustrative rebate true-up table (US-only for year 1; optional EU activation in year 2). I will include a line that shows seat fees moved into consumption and the alternate +3% rebate scenario for 99.9 uptime.
2) Legal: Ben's redline includes a proposed uplift to the annual credit cap for a committed deal; please review and flag any concerns.
3) Ops: Rishi to confirm whether we can offer named-engineer rotation for the account size; if yes we'll propose a short appendix with handoff/backup rules.

Can you confirm by Wednesday whether Acme prefers the staged expansion approach and whether counsel wants the higher annual credit cap so we can finalize the DocuSign draft? I'm happy to schedule a 30-minute call with Ben and Rishi if your team would prefer to talk through the exhibit.

Best,
Marissa
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
